author: reek
body: The constructor-pattern memory read: `LiLoad`, the last per-construct arm of the ARM64 LIR selector (LirRetarget step 4i). A `when s is Circle (r) -> ...` lowers to a load of the variant tag from `[sv + 0]`, a compare against the constructor's tag, a branch, and then one load per bound field at its packed offset and width. Everything but the loads was already whitelisted by steps 4e and 4g, so this file is what the last arm buys.

author: reek
body: Pinned by ANSWERS, because the two lanes reach them by different instructions and the answers are what must agree. x86-64 selects these through `lir-sel-load`; the ARM64 plug selects them through `a64-lir-emit-load`; the tree emitter behind both would also answer correctly, which is why the sensitivity run rather than the green is what proves the LIR path claimed them.

author: reek
body: **A constructor APPLICATION is not lowerable and a constructor PATTERN is.** The lowering declines `Circle 5`, so every function here takes its variant as a parameter and `opening` builds the values on the tree path. That split is not an accident of the test: it is what makes these functions reachable by the selector at all.

author: reek
body: A variant whose every field is eight bytes wide, which is what the first increment admits: pointers, unbounded integers and sum payloads are all width eight, and `arm64-ldr` covers them with no new encoding.

author: reek
body: `Dot` carries no fields, so its arm tests the tag and loads nothing. `Rect` carries two, so the second sits at offset 16 and is the only shape here that reads past the first field slot.

author: reek
body: Every arm reads a field, and the nullary arm reads none. A wrong tag load sends every call to the wrong arm; a wrong field offset answers a neighbour.

author: reek
body: The first field alone, from two different constructors, so offset 8 is read under two different tags.

author: reek
body: The second field, at offset 16. This is the row that separates a load whose offset is honoured from one that always reads the first slot: `sh-first` and `sh-second` on the same `Rect` must disagree.

author: reek
body: A wildcard arm rather than an exhaustive constructor list, and a bound field used twice in the arm body, so the loaded vreg outlives its defining instruction.

author: reek
body: Both fields of one constructor in one expression, so two loads are live at once and the allocator has to keep them apart.

target: section:The narrow shapes, which must decline
author: reek
body: A field narrower than eight bytes is NOT whitelisted in this increment: the encoder has `arm64-ldr` (8), `arm64-ldrb` (1 unsigned) and `arm64-ldr-w` (4 zero-extending) and lacks every sign-extending narrow form, so admitting narrow widths is a separate change with its own encodings. These two functions exist to prove the gate declines rather than emitting an eight-byte load over a one-byte field.
